Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gasThe Trump administration wants to undo a Biden-era rule that would reduce methane emissions from the oil and gas industry.
Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas
Flares burn off methane and other hydrocarbons at an oil and gas facility in Lenorah, Texas, Oct. 15, 2021.David Goldman/APhide caption
The Trump administration is proposing to dramatically scale back a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut methane emissions from the oil and gas industry at drilling sites nationwide.
Methane is a major contributor to climate change and is estimated to be 80 times more planet-warming than carbon dioxide in a twenty-year time frame. In 2023, the Biden administration finalized rules that were meant to rein in methane emissions from the oil and gas sector.
President Trump made the announcement while campaigning in Lubbock, Texas, Tuesday, saying his administration's revision, under the Clean Air Act, would save the industry billions in production costs and spur more domestic drilling. The proposal comes as Republicans face a backlash from voters over high gas prices heading into the midterms.
"Behind every barrel of oil and every cubic foot of natural gas produced in the U.S. are millions of workers, businesses, and the heartbeat of this nation's economy. The Biden EPA destructively targeted all this," EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin said in a press release.
The oil and gas industry, which vigorously opposed the 2023 rules, said EPA's proposed rollback will address some of the challenges companies have faced in trying to comply with the regulations.
"We look forward to working with the Trump administration on a more workable approach that supports American energy production, provides greater regulatory certainty and advances continued emissions reductions," Dustin Meyer, vice president at the American Petroleum Institute, a trade organization for the U.S. oil and gas industry, said in a statement.
But environmentalists say this may end up actually costing the industry more.
"Methane is natural gas, or natural gas is methane," says Jon Goldstein, associate vice president at the Environmental Defense Fund. "And so if you're capturing more natural gas, you're not allowing it to leak out, you're not allowing it to be flared, you have more product that you can sell. And so that offsets a lot of the costs."
"That is harmful to our energy security, and it's harmful to taxpayers that ought to be seeing royalty and tax revenue collected off of this gas that's going to waste," Goldstein adds.
One of the regulations the EPA wants to cut is the "Methane Super Emitter Program." Across the U.S., oil and gas pipelines, refineries, and other energy facilities sometimes have huge leaks of methane. But methane is invisible and difficult, not to mention expensive, to detect. The super emitter program is supposed to take effect in January 2027. It would allow the government to delegate monitoring for big methane leaks to certified third parties, including private and nonprofit methane satellite programs.
New satellite is designed to track methane emitted from the oil and gas industry
"The easiest way to think about it is that if the government is alerted to a big leak, then if it's reported by certified third parties, then they could use that information," says Paasha Mahdavi, a political science professor at UC Santa Barbara who studies the oil industry.
"[The government] needs help from other people to say, 'Hey! You're breaking the law!' so they're able to prosecute," Mahdavi adds.
If that program goes away, Mahdavi says it will be harder for the government to spot large leaks of the planet-heating gas from oil and gas facilities. "And we need that because it's really hard to see this stuff," he says.
The EPA's announcement would also loosen regulations on methane leaks coming from low-volume "marginal" oil wells that are considered "marginally economic," meaning they don't make much money.
Why a tiny bit of oil can be a big deal
"People assume marginal well must equal small emissions," Goldstein says. But he says satellites and new technology find that's not true. "These old sort of end-of-life wells nearing the end of their production life are actually responsible for the lion's share of methane pollution from the [oil and gas] production sector," Goldstein says.
The EPA plans to hold at least a 45-day public comment period, including a public hearing, once the proposed rule changes are published in theFederal Register.

Ciara Mageean, European 1500m gold medallist with Ireland, dies aged 34
Mageean won 2024 European 1500m title in Rome
Athlete described as ‘an inspiration to many’
Irish middle-distance runner Ciara Mageean, who won European gold and competed at two Olympic Games, has died aged 34, her family have announced.
The athlete, from Portaferry, Northern Ireland, died at 6.30am on Sunday. In a post on social media, her family said she was surrounded by her loved ones. They said: “A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed.”
Mageean was one of the most high-profile athletes in Ireland, specialising in the 1500m event. She represented Ireland at both the 2016 Rio Olympics and 2020 Tokyo Olympics, as well as holding a slew of Irish records.
She went on to become the first individual Irish European champion since Sonia O’Sullivan when she struck gold at the 2024 championships in Rome. Mageean was unable to compete at the 2024 Olympics due to an achilles injury.
The following year, Mageean announced she had been diagnosed with cancer. She went on to marry her partner Thomas Moran in October only weeks before her death.
Taoiseach Micheál Martin said he was deeply saddened at her untimely passing. “My heartfelt sympathies go to her husband Thomas, all her family and friends,” he said. Tánaiste Simon Harris described the news as heartbreaking. He said: “She was a European champion, two-time Olympian, a proud Irish athlete and an extraordinary person.”
Northern Ireland’s first minister, Michelle O’Neill, said Mageean demonstrated “extraordinary talent, determination and dedication.” She said: “I am deeply saddened to hear of the passing of Ciara Mageean, and I want to extend my heartfelt condolences to her husband Tommy, her parents, family, friends and everyone who loved her.
“Ciara’s achievements in athletics brought immense pride to her local community and to people right across Ireland. From representing Ireland at two Olympic Games to winning European Championship gold in Rome in 2024, Ciara demonstrated extraordinary talent, determination and dedication.
“However, beyond the medals, records and sporting accolades, Ciara will be remembered for her warmth, courage and tremendous strength of character. Throughout her illness, she showed a remarkable spirit and an incredible ability to find hope and joy in life, even in the most difficult circumstances. Her courage touched countless people and will leave a lasting legacy.
View image in fullscreenCiara Mageean (left) competing for Northern Ireland at the 2022 Commonwealth Games.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA
“For a community like Portaferry, this loss will be deeply felt. Ciara was one of our own, and the pride she brought to her community and beyond will never be forgotten. At this incredibly difficult time, I hope her family and loved ones can take some comfort from knowing just how deeply she was admired, respected and loved by so many people.”
Deputy first minister Emma Little-Pengelly said: “I am so sorry to hear of the death of Ciara Mageean, at the age of 34 years. An outstanding athlete and ambassador for her sport, Ciara was born in Portaferry, County Down, and represented Northern Ireland and predominantly Ireland on the world stage.
“Ciara had outstanding success, and was an inspiration to many. She spoke with such honesty and bravery about the health battles she subsequently faced. I know so many from right across Northern Ireland were deeply proud and inspired by Ciara. My deepest condolences to her family, teammates and friends, and her husband to whom she had so recently married.”

Mageean became a European champion in 2024
Former European champion and two-time Olympian Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34.
Mageean, from Portaferry in Northern Ireland, was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer in May 2025.
She represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics, but was forced to withdraw from the 2024 Paris Games because of an Achilles injury.
Earlier in 2024, Mageean had clinched the first major title of her career when she took1500m gold at the European Championships in Rome.
Prior to that she had also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning 1500m silver at Birmingham 2022.
A statement posted on her social media on Sunday said: "At 6.30am this morning, Ciara lost her battle with cancer surrounded by her loved ones.
"A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed.
"Ar dheis Dé go raibh a hanam (may her soul rest in peace)."
In a statement on social media, Athletics Ireland said: "We are heartbroken. An inspiration to so many, Ciara will be remembered for her courage, kindness and incredible spirit.
"Our deepest sympathies are with her family, friends and loved ones at this difficult time. Rest in peace, Ciara."
In October, Mageeanwed her long-term partner Thomas Moranin a small civil ceremony in Belfast.
A talented athlete from a young age, Mageean played camogie for Portaferry GAC, but her dream of representing Ireland at the Olympics led her to pursue a career in athletics.
Her running prowess was clear during an impressive junior career that yielded 1500m silvers at the 2010 World Junior Championships and 2011 European Junior Championships. She also reached the 2010 Commonwealth Games 1500m final as an 18-year-old.
However, Mageean's early progress in the senior ranks was hampered by a serious ankle injury, which ended her hopes of making her Olympic debut at London 2012.
Having had surgery in 2013, Mageean won the Irish 1500m title on her return in July 2014.
In 2016, she claimed 1500m bronze at the European Championships in Amsterdam, but her Olympic debut ended in disappointment as she exited the 1500m competition at the semi-final stage.
In late 2017, Mageean left her Dublin base to join Steve Vernon's Team New Balance in Manchester after parting ways with coach Jerry Kiernan.
And while she endured some disappointing results following the move, Mageean claimed a European Indoor bronze medal in March 2019 before clocking two minutes 31.06 seconds to take 3.6 seconds off Sonia O'Sullivan's 27-year-old Irish 1,000m record at the2020 Diamond League Monaco meet.
Mageean won a gold medal at the 2024 European Championships in Rome
Mageean endured more Olympic heartache at the delayed Tokyo Games in 2021, when a calf injury disrupted her preparations as she exited from the heats.
However, she enjoyed a successful 2022 campaign under the guidance of former Great Britain Olympian Helen Clitheroe, winning 1500m European and Commonwealth silver behind Laura Muir.
Two weeks after the Euros, Mageean beat Muir and a world-class field to seal a stunning 1500m victory at Diamond League Brussels. Her time of 3:56.63 took 2.22 seconds off O'Sullivan's Irish record and marked her first sub four-minute run.
In 2023, Mageean narrowly missed out on a World Championship medal as she finished fourth in a high-class final in Budapest.
However, after taking over two seconds off O'Sullivan's Irish mile record in July, Mageean was named the 2023 BBC Northern Ireland Sports Personality of the Year.
Ireland's Mageean takes 1500m gold as GB's Bell wins silver
After a string of near-misses at championship level, Mageean secured the biggest win of her career at the 2024 European Championships in Rome.
In a gripping final, Mageean found herself boxed in behind Great Britain duo Georgia Bell and Jemma Reekie, but managed to dart through a gap and power down the straight to victory in 4:04.66.
An ecstatic Mageean, who won admirers for her honest and emotional post-race interviews down the years, said "words can't even come close" to describing how she felt after sealing the first major title of her career.
After Mageean's jubilation in Rome, injury again interrupted her Olympic bid as an Achilles injury forced her to withdraw on the eve of her heat in Paris.
Earlier this year, Mageean said she was "continuing to find the joy in everyday" as she thanked people for their support following her diagnosis.
Speaking to the BBC in June,she saidshe was "grateful" for having a career "that many others didn't get to have".

White Dwarfs Aren’t Just White. Scientists Discover Dying Stars Turning Pink and Green | WIREDSkip to main content
The realm ofstars resembles a fairy tale. In it, we find giants, supergiants, and also many dwarfs. Rather like the flames of a fire, most stars’ colors are based on temperature. Cooler stars look orange, sun-like stars appear white, and the hottest ones shine light blue. However, there are exceptions, and astronomers have recently discovered some among the class of stars known aswhite dwarfs.
At theend of their lives, stars with a mass similar to the sun expand and turn into red giants. Subsequently, they shed theirgaseous envelope, creating a planetary nebula that we can admire through telescopes. In place of the star, a white dwarf remains—a highly condensed object the approximate volume of the Earth butthe massof the sun.
Initially, white dwarfs have extremely high temperatures, and so the first ones discovered shone from white to light blue. That’s how they got their name. But according to a new study published in the journalRAS Techniques and Instruments, the world of white dwarfs is actually far more colorful—with some stars turning pink, green, and even purple.
The researchers posit that density is the deciding factor. The atmospheres of the coolest white dwarfs can reach a density of approximately 1 gram per cubic centimeter. That’s roughly the same density as water, which may not sound like much, but it’s packed for a star, this being about a million times denser thanthe sun’s atmosphere. Under these conditions, anytrace elementslike carbon, calcium, and sodium interact with the surrounding dense helium plasma and absorb light across a wider range of colors.
Material from ancient planetary systems also plays a role. The closest planets can perish in thefiery embraceof the red giant phase. Other planets, and especially asteroids, beginto collideand migrate toward the dead star. Fragments of these bodies then integrate into the white dwarf's atmosphere.
Through a hobbyist’s telescope, a white dwarf looks just like any other faint star. However, if observed up close, their colors would be much more varied. Carbon-rich white dwarfs tend to be pink or purple. According to calculations, white dwarfswhose atmosphereshave been enriched with material from shattered asteroids or other bodies will exhibit yellow and, in some cases, green shades. The coolest white dwarfs are often a baby blue, which is caused by hydrogen and heliumatoms collidingin their extremely dense atmospheres.
One example is the star WD J1330+6435. With a temperature of around 4,000 degrees Celsius, it has accumulated rocky material from its planetary system, enriching its atmosphere with calcium, lithium, and sodium. These elements give it a light chartreuse color, making it the first known green star inour galaxy.
Another white dwarf, WD J1011+2845, has a massive amount of carbon in its atmosphere. Almost all of its radiation is concentrated at wavelengths exceeding 600 nanometers, giving it a salmon-pink color. Meanwhile, the white dwarf WD J902-2010 leans toward the more bubblegum end of the spectrum.
However, there’s no reason to expect white dwarfs to start getting renamed, because most of these stars are, in fact, white. For this study, the authors examined 152 white dwarfs locatedwithin 65 light-yearsof Earth. Only five of them showed unusual coloration, suggesting that approximately one in thirty white dwarfs in the universe shines with unusually colored light.
This might seem like an expected result, but scientists previously assumed that white dwarfs were predominantly blue. That assumption may reflect bias insampling the night sky. The hottest white dwarfs are also typically the brightest and can, therefore, be seen from greater distances. Because they’reeasier to observe, many studies end up over-representing blue stars.
While you won’t be able to see the nearest white dwarf with the naked eye either, you can at least look in its direction. Sirius B is the companion to the brightest star in Earth’s night sky. During winter, Sirius is easy to spot shining brightly above the eastern horizon. Sirius B belongs to the group of “more boring” white dwarfs—its temperature hovers around 25,000 Kelvin, giving it a light blue color.

Rampant Australia racked up the biggest score in international history as they hammered Wales in a Rugby League World Cup mismatch.
The Jillaroos, hunting a fourth successive title, ran in 21 tries in a predictably lopsided contest in Sydney.
The half-time score of 60-0 was the biggest of any World Cup match - men's or women's - and the Australians kept their foot down to win 124-6.
Wing Jaime Chapman's sixth try in the last minute ensured they beat Denmark men's biggest international score of 122-8 against Sweden in 2012.
The 118-point victory margin is the largest in any women's match, although France men retain their record win set in 2003 with a 120-0 rout of Serbia.
Yet there were wild Wales celebrations when, at 100-0 down, they became the first side to score against the Jillaroos in the tournament through Paige Travis.
Australia, Papua New Guinea, New Zealand

The Jillaroos are three-time back-to-back champions, while Wales were taking part in the tournament for the first time having only played their first Test in 2021.
It was just their 16th fixture - and a first against Australia - with Tom Brindle's side having already been beaten70-6 by Englandand76-0 by Samoaat the World Cup.
Full of NRLW talent, Australia showed a killer instinct and an intensity that Wales were exposed to for the first time.

Long-striding, hard-fending Chapman scored a double down the left and fellow wing Abbi Church powered through weak tackles on the right.

Sergis brought up the half-century with a weaving run and was followed over by second row Sariah Paki.

The Jillaroos beat their 92-0 record, set against France in the 2022 World Cup, when Southwell converted Sergis' fourth try, hitting three figures when the extras were added to star full-back Tamika Upton's breakaway.

It was only a brief change of pattern with Keeley Nizza, Chapman twice and Upton going over to complete the destruction.

There’s a Free Video Editor Inside Google Drive That Anyone Can Use | WIREDSkip to main content
Mention the onlineapps available as part of Google Workspace, and most people will immediately think ofGoogle Drive,Gmail,Google Docs, Google Sheets, and Google Slides—those speedy, lightweight office apps that let you get work done from any browser tab.
There's more to the suite of Google Workspace tools than you might have realized though, including an online video editing package calledGoogle Vids. Originally launched in 2024 for business and enterprise users, the app was made available to individuals in 2026 and continues toget regular updatesfrom Google.
Since it's both free to use and designed to run in a web browser, it's not capable of pro-level, high-resolution, multitrack video editing. But for personal and hobbyist use, it works well, and it won't take you long to learn the basics.
Finding Google Vids isn't difficult: You can either open Google Driveon the web, then clickNewandGoogle Vids, or head straight tothe Google Vids apppage and click the+(plus) button underStart a new video.(Any videos you've previously made are shown here, too.)
Besides beginning with a clean state (theBlank vidoption), there are plenty of other ways to get started: You can generate AI videos with the Veo 3.1 model, turn a slideshow into a video, work from a template, upload an existing video as a starting point, create an AI music track, record a video using your camera, produce a video with an AI avatar, or create a storyboard outline. Note you can also pick the video orientation at the top.
There are numerous options for getting started.Courtesy of David Nield
Most of these options use a similar layout, and we're going to focus on the traditional video-making approach here—though the AI options are well worth exploring, too, if you don't have source material to work with. If you're new to Google Vids, then pickingTemplatesfrom the opening splash screen will ease you in gently.
When it comes to picking a template, the topic isn't as important as the layout. Look for something that matches what you want to create as closely as possible (hover over any of the thumbnails to see an animated preview). The next dialog lets you choose whether you want to use the entire template or just selected scenes. After that, you're into the video editing interface proper.
Most of the elements should be relatively familiar if you've ever used a timeline-based video editor in the past. At the bottom you've got your video and audio tracks, while the main window shows the currently selected segment of your video. The panel on the right lets you edit whatever's currently selected.
The timeline sits at the bottom, with the current scene above.Courtesy of David Nield
Down the right side of the interface you've got all the options for loading in new content. You can record webcam clips, create AI videos, import footage from Google Drive and Google Photos, add voiceovers, and drop in text, images, music, and shapes. If you've started with a template, some of these elements will be styled to match.
Along the top of the Google Vids interface are more editing and formatting tools. These menus are where you should head to change transitions between scenes, to manage how elements are arranged in a particular scene, to drop in new scenes, and to manage your video project as a whole.
Building Video Projects With Google Vids
To begin building your projects, you'll probably want to load in audio, video, and images via the buttons on the right. On the most basic level, you can click the+(plus) button on the timeline to create a new scene, then drag in a photo or video from the right-hand panel to fill the scene you've just created.
A whole host of options present themselves when you right-click on the timeline. You can, for example, mute the audio track imported with a video, then add a voiceover or some different music. You're also able to split scenes (if you only want to keep half a scene maybe) and duplicate scenes (for quickly expanding the running time of your project) with a right-click.
Keep your eye on the panel on the right, which changes depending on the context. With audio tracks, you can apply fades, and with video clips you can choose from different transitions. If your scene has several elements (like shapes that scroll over a video), you're able to adjust how they look and behave.
Let's say you have a video scene and want to put some text over it. Select the scene in the timeline, click theTextbutton on the right, then clickAdd a titleto do just that. If you then select the title in the scene itself, you can change the text and its styling.
Using the handles around the text box you can change its position, size, and rotation. There are also three buttons underneath on a floating toolbar:Animationlets you animate the text,Resizewill resize the text box to fit the text you've entered, andFormat optionsbrings up a panel where you can change text size, padding, rotation, and so on.
You can also make use of stock images, videos, and audio if needed.Courtesy of David Nield
Click and drag on elements inside a scene to reposition them, and right-click for more options—includingCut,Copy,Paste, andDelete. If you need more material to work with, choose the Stock option on the right, which gives you a library of material you can make use of in addition to your own content and anything created with AI.
There's a lot more to Google Vids, but that should be enough to get you started—try experimenting with a few of the templates to see what else is possible. As with the other Google Drive apps, all your edits are saved instantly, and up in the top right corner you've got aPlaybutton for viewing your work in progress, and aSharebutton for when it’s ready for the world to see.

Image source,Getty ImagesByKevin PeacheyCost of living correspondent
Families facing cost-of-living pressures are being offered some help, or "breathing space" as Chancellor John Healey is calling it.
The help comes as prices are rising faster than expected with annual energy bills in particular likely to increase by hundreds of pounds in January.
Here's how the key announcements in the Budget affect you and your money.
If you are living in a home in council tax bands A to D in England, you will receive a one-off £100 "Household Energy Payment" from January, funded by extra tax on banks.
It will be paid directly into your bank account.
Council tax bands are listed below - you can check which one you are in by looking at your annual bill or checkingthe government's website,external, although that was struggling to cope with traffic after the announcement.
Administrations in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive the equivalent funding, and they will decide whether to introduce the same payment.
This is designed to help with soaring energy bills, with some forecasts suggesting a typical annual bill could rise by £400 or so to £2,100 in January the saving will be only a portion of that. Although it's designated for energy bills, you can spend the money on anything you wish.
The VAT cut on electricity bills, which was introduced in October, will also be extended to July. It was due to end in April.
The fee for connecting to your gas supply so called standing charges will be scrapped in England, Scotland and Wales, next year "or as soon as possible after", the chancellor said.
These fixed daily charges will then be shifted onto the price you pay for each unit of energy.
The Treasury calculates that 60% of households will save an average of £45 a year, with lower users gaining the most. But the saving will come after the projected big rise in bills in January.
Higher users - in the biggest houses but also large, low-income families - will pay more than they currently do.
The government wants to extend reforms to electricity standing charges later.
The 5p "temporary" cut in fuel duty on petrol and diesel, introduced by Rishi Sunak in 2022, will be extended to July. It was scheduled to be phased out from January.
It means drivers will still pay the levy at 52.95p per litre.
Motor fuel prices have risen sharply owing to the continued impact of the Iran war on drivers, with diesel having recently hit new records when it moved above £2 per litre.
The cost of filling a typical family car with diesel has gone up by around £30 since late February. A tankful of petrol costs about £23 more.
The chancellor has scrapped his predecessor's plans to reduce the annual amount people can save tax-free in cash in Individual Savings Accounts (Isas).
Rachel Reeves had wanted the policy to encourage personal investment in stocks and shares.
It meant, from April 2027, if you're under 65, you would only be able to save £12,000 a year in cash in an Isa, rather than £20,000.
Instead, the government plans to create a new "Starter Isa" for first-time investors.
More tax for some savers and landlords
If you have a large amount in savings, or if you fail to use the tax-free Isa allowance, then you will pay more tax from April.
You do not pay tax on all savings. There is the annual £20,000 Isa allowance, and an annual savings income allowance (in other words, the interest received on a savings pot) of £1,000 for basic rate taxpayers and £500 for higher-rate taxpayers.
But beyond that savings tax rates will rise by four percentage points to 24% and 44% respectively from April.
Landlords could also pay more in tax. In analysis published on Wednesday, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said these steps along with measures over the past decade that have reduced private landlord returns "collectively risk leading to a steady rise in rents".
Minimum wage rise but you'll pay more tax
Minimum wage rates will rise by 3.9% in April. It means:
Eligible workers aged 21 and over on the National Living Wage will receive £13.21 an hour, up from £12.71
If you are aged 18, 19 or 20, the National Minimum Wage will increase to £11.27 an hour, up from £10.85
For those aged 16 or 17, the minimum wage will rise to £8.31 an hour, up from £8
The separate apprentice rate which applies to eligible people under 19 - or those over 19 in the first year of an apprenticeship – will also increase to £8.31 an hour, from £8
However, these figures mean, this time around, there's no progress on Labour's manifesto promise to narrow the gap in minimum wages between older and younger workers.
For all workers,the ongoing freeze in the income bands, or thresholds, at which income tax is paid went unmentioned in the Budget.
But it means any kind of pay rise could drag you into a higher tax bracket, or see a greater proportion of your income taxed than would otherwise be expected. Scotland has its own income tax bands.
How much is the minimum wage going up by?
The triple lock policy means that the state pension will go up in line with average wage increases, at 3.9%.
the flat-rate state pension for those who reached state pension age after April 2016 will be £250.70 a week, or £13,036.40 a year, up £488 on now
the old basic state pension for those who reached state pension age before April 2016 will be £192.10 a week, or £9,989.20 a year, up £374.40 on now
The government had already committed to not taxing people who only get an income from the state pension.
The chancellor said this would be the case until at least 2030, as there will be a new Pension Tax Allowance, so pensioners with an income up to the value of the full new state pension will not pay income tax.
The First Time Buyer Isa has been in the planning stages with the government for a while.
Healey has confirmed that it is intended to replace the often-criticised Lifetime Isa.
The penalty for withdrawing savings from a Lifetime Isa if you are buying a home above the £450,000 threshold will be scrapped.

J-PAL North America launches ARTEMIS to train early-career researchers
The Applied Research Training in Evaluation, Methods, and Impact Studies program provides dedicated support to help researchers overcome barriers to pursue and obtain funding for randomized evaluations.Katherine Rodriguez Marquez|J-PAL North AmericaPublication Date:October 30, 2026Press Inquiries
ErinGraeberEmail:egraeber@povertyactionlab.orgPhone:617-324-6916Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action LabCloseCaption:J-PAL North America's inaugural ARTEMIS cohort attended Summer Institute — an intensive week-long course at the MIT Endicott House — to begin their training last June.Credits:Photo courtesy of J-PAL North America.
The Applied Research Training in Evaluation, Methods, and Impact Studies (ARTEMIS) program, launched by J-PAL North America, equips early-career researchers with high-level technical training and practical skills to design randomized evaluations (also referred to as a randomized controlled trials, or RCTs) on issues of poverty in the U.S. context. Fully funded and highly rigorous, the program's inaugural cohort of 20 participants — including PhD students through pre-tenure faculty — is receiving training, mentorship, and proposal development support through December.
ARTEMIS is the newest offering within J-PAL North America’s Economics Pathways program, which broadens and strengthens the pipeline of economics researchers by providing support to aspiring scholars at every stage — from undergraduate interns to research staff and, now, academic researchers preparing to launch their first randomized evaluations.
ARTEMIS programming commenced this past June with the Summer Institute — an intensive weeklong course at MIT Endicott House in Dedham, Massachusetts, that focused on delivering technical content and building participants' practical skills and confidence to design and pursue funding for rigorous evaluations to address poverty in the United States. During the Summer Institute, participants had the opportunity to learn from researchers in the J-PAL network, including Gerald Daniels,associate professor of economicsat Howard University, who served as a lecturer for the program. “ARTEMIS is an amazing program that bridges the gap for researchers who haven't previously had the opportunity to work with randomized evaluations,” notes Daniels. “It takes rigorous methodologies, like randomized evaluations, and makes them approachable, helping scholars translate their research ideas into high-impact evaluation designs."
The inaugural cohort brought together early-career researchers from institutions across the United States, each tackling a research question addressing an issue related to poverty that is well-suited for a randomized evaluation. Their interests spanned the breadth of J-PAL’s work, touching on education, climate, health and labor markets, racial equity, and social protection — reflecting the wide range of policy questions that rigorous, evidence-based research can help answer.
“I really appreciated being a part of the ARTEMIS Institute this summer,” says Felipe Juan, an ARTEMIS inaugural cohort participant. “I initially thought the randomized evaluation methodology would be out of reach for me, but the summer training helped to break down the practical steps of conducting an RCT and identify creative ways to approach experimental designs.”
Bolstered by the intensive Summer Institute training, ARTEMIS participants are now engaging in six months of continued study design and proposal development support, including proposal webinars with J-PAL grants staff and office hours with senior technical staff who will advise on study design and proposal challenges. ARTEMIS participants will also participate in a research design workshop, where participants present their early-stage RCT designs and receive feedback from the broader J-PAL research network. Finally, participants will receive introductions to researchers in the J-PAL network with shared research interests to forge connections that may lead to future collaboration and opportunities. Through this sustained mentorship model, ARTEMIS is designed to help participants bridge the gap between developing a promising research idea and launching a funded, policy-relevant randomized evaluation.
For early-career researchers, this hands-on, sustained support has already proven to be transformative. “Participating in ARTEMIS Summer Institute was an incredibly valuable experience. The combination of lectures by experts in the design and implementation of randomized controlled trials, hands-on workshops, and thoughtful feedback helped me sharpen my research questions and think more carefully about research design, implementation, statistical power, and meaningful stakeholder engagement,” says Hoyoung Yoo, an ARTEMIS 2026 participant. “I also greatly appreciated the opportunity to learn from J-PAL faculty and staff and exchange ideas with an inspiring group of fellow researchers. I left the training with a clearer path toward transforming an early-stage idea into a feasible, rigorous, and policy-relevant evaluation.”
For many, the program’s value also extends beyond technical training to the community and long-term relationships it builds. “J-PAL North America’s support has continued well beyond the Summer Institute, which has been especially valuable, and the connections I made have already started shaping how I am approaching the work,” notes Tessie Krishna, an ARTEMIS 2026 participant. “I left with a clearer proposal, a wider network, and a real sense of belonging in the J-PAL community. I am grateful to the J-PAL team for creating something so thoughtful and welcoming.”
By building the technical capacity and confidence of the next generation of researchers, ARTEMIS is advancing J-PAL’s global mission to reduce poverty by ensuring that policy is informed by rigorous, scientific evidence. Every individual trained through ARTEMIS is joining a growing network of researchers working to answer the most critical questions of today.

Microsoft is beginning the rollout of a Windows 11 preview update that finally addresses a persistent power user complaint with the operating system: the right-click menu that obliterated years of muscle memory on command locations and hid others behind an additional click. The timing is notable, as the announcement comes alongside Microsoft’s quarterly financial report, which showed a continued decline in the business of selling Windows licenses for new PCs.
The preview update,KB5127936, is cumulative for Windows 11 versions 26H2 and 25H2. The update will be a gradual rollout before eventually moving on to a normal rollout for all Windows 11 devices once it reaches general availability. The highlight of the new update should calm annoyed users who have spent years with custom scripts and services in an attempt to shape Windows the way they would prefer it. Users will get a “customize menu” button that controls what commands appear when they right-click their mouse. Users can toggle built-in commands such as Send To or Create Shortcut on or off, rearrange what appears on the main menu, and control which third-party extensions show up in either the main or submenus. The gripe with the right-click menu had been that Microsoft hid familiar command locations behind a top row of icons while moving other familiar commands under the “Show more options” submenu. Now, Windows users can customize the whole thing around their habits.
The original Windows 11 right-click menu is a mess.Credit:MicrosoftThe original Windows 11 right-click menu is a mess.Credit:Microsoft
The new preview also highlights a new Windows feature called Cloud Rebuild, a recovery option that can reinstall Windows 11 directly from the cloud, even when an existing Windows 11 fails to boot. Cloud Rebuild will pull the Windows 11 image and needed system drivers directly from Windows Update. Users will not need a custom recovery image or external media to reinstall Windows. There is an important distinction to note, however. Microsoft classifies Cloud Rebuild as a recovery option, but it behaves more like a fresh Windows install than a repair, as existing applications and files will not be included. Those worried about data security can sanitize entire system drives prior to reinstalling. For a full list of improvements coming to Windows 11, including changes to Xbox mode and settings, you can view the officialMicrosoft release announcement.
Microsoft’s latest quarterly report, released this week, paints a less encouraging picture of its Windows OEM business. “Windows OEM revenue was below expectations and decreased 27% and 28% in constant currency, driven by the Windows 10 end of support demand in the prior year, inventory drawdowns by OEM and channel partners and weaker PC market demand,” said CFO Amy Hood, according to atranscript of the call. The broader Windows OEM and devices category, which includes Microsoft’s own Surface lineup, fell 22 percent, per the earnings release. Hood went on to state that “we expect these trends to continue through the rest of the fiscal year.”
Recent hardware efforts like theSurface Laptop Ultraand broader RTX Spark platform arrived too late in the quarter to register in the results, and Microsoft forecastfurther dropsbefore any possible boost from new hardware can show in its numbers. The news for Microsoft isn’t negative all around, though, as its Azure platform saw a 48 percent jump, and Microsoft Cloud revenue was also up 30 percent, year over year—now roughly 70 percent of the company’s $92.3 billion total quarterly revenue.

ByVanessa Buschschlüter,Latin America and Caribbean editor,Ione Wells,North America correspondentandMax Matza
Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who landed in Miami after losing the presidential election on Sunday, has said it was never his intention to "leave my homeland".
"I did not flee Brazil; I left for the sake of Brazil," he said in his first statement since his departure.
The US provided visas to him and his family after Brazil cancelled his passports as part of a criminal investigation. Bolsonaro denies any wrongdoing. On Wednesday, US President Donald Trump told reporters: "We gave him a pass to come into the country".
Newly re-elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva hascriticised Bolsonaro's secretive exit from the country, saying "those who have nothing to hide have nothing to fear".
Watch: Bolsonaro shielded from media by umbrellas at Florida airport
Bolsonaro's arrival in Florida ended days of confusion over his whereabouts, after he was reported to have travelled to Argentina, and then prematurely reported to have already entered the US on Tuesday.
In a statement, Bolsonaro thanked both the presidents of Argentina and the US, and the American public "who share the same values ​​as the good people of my own country".
"It was never my intention to leave my homeland, but I know exactly where this is heading," he said. "I departed from a regime of exception so that I could become the leader my people deserve."
He called himself a victim of a coup d'état and political persecution, and said his travel to the US was to protect his family.
In the lengthy letter, he also repeated unsubstantiated allegations of "electoral fraud" which he said allowed a "mathematical impossibility" to occur in the election.
On Wednesday, Trump declined to discuss the allegations made in Bolsonaro's letter.
"I won't get involved. It was a very strange election, that's for sure," Trump said. He went on to add that he thought Bolsonaro "and his family were treated very unfairly".
After Bolsonaro won the first round of Brazil's election, Lula won the second round by more than four million votes, which was attributed to significantly higher turnout, and swaying more undecided voters.
The result was confirmed by the president of Brazil's top electoral court, who was appointed by Bolsonaro's father, former president Jair Bolsonaro.
Speculation about Bolsonaro's whereabouts was first triggered by a report on an Argentine news site, which claimed that he had crossed the land border between Brazil and Argentina and then boarded a private plane en route to the US.
Brazilian police took the rumours seriously. Early on Tuesday, they checked border crossings but found no evidence that Bolsonaro had left the country, and Argentine officials said they had no reports of him crossing.
For a little while, it seemed like Bolsonaro may just be keeping an uncharacteristically low-profile after being unexpectedly beaten by his left-wing rival in the presidential run-off vote on Sunday, in addition to a criminal investigation that led to orders that his passports be turned into authorities.
But when he failed to surrender his passports in time to meet a 24-hour deadline on Tuesday, Brazilian authorities cancelled the documents and ordered police to make checks at border posts.
Speculation quickly grew that he'd left the country and Bolsonaro's lawyers said they had no idea where he was.
How did Flávio Bolsonaro end up in Miami?
Confusion about Bolsonaro's whereabouts as Argentina says he flew to Ecuador
Hours later on Tuesday evening, several sources told the BBC and other broadcasters that he was on his way to the US.
A cousin, who is close to Flávio Bolsonaro and his younger brother Eduardo, told BBC Brasil that the defeated right-wing candidate had arrived in Miami.
Another close aide to Eduardo Bolsonaro told BBC Mundo that Flávio was with his younger brother in Miami.
Neither Flávio nor Eduardo Bolsonaro could be reached directly for comment at the time.
But later, however, Argentine migration authorities posted on social media saying that Bolsonaro, his wife, and two daughters had only just crossed into Argentina over land on Tuesday night local time.
Flight tracking data verified by the BBC suggested the Bolsonaros departed from Puerto Iguazú in Argentina at 00:18 local time (03:18 GMT) on Wednesday to head to Guayaquil in Ecuador.
After a brief stop, the same private jet took them to Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport, where they were pictured disembarking just before 09:30 local time (13:30 GMT).
Photographers, who had been waiting for his arrival to finally put an end to all the speculation, swarmed around Bolsonaro as he left the airport in Miami, while his team tried to cover him with umbrellas.
Later, Eduardo Bolsonaro posted a photo with his brother Flávio on social media, with the location listed as "United States".
The caption read: "Today's photo after reuniting with my brother Flavio Bolsonaro. Yesterday was a long day, perhaps the longest of my life. But we prevailed. Even here outside, we will not give up on Brazil."

Democrats have high hopes for midterms, but polls have let them down before - BBC News
Image source,Getty ImagesByAnthony ZurcherNorth America correspondent
The Democratic Party has high expectations as it heads into these pivotal US midterm elections.
A historically unpopular Republican president, an American public unhappy with the rising costs of food and bills, and months of favourable polls point to a good night for them on Tuesday.
Democratic candidates lead in well over the 218 seats needed to flip control of the lower chamber of Congress, the House of Representatives, the polls suggest. And they are tied or narrowly ahead in the key Senate races.
A recent New York Times poll had the Senate race in South Carolina, a state Donald Trump won by 18 percentage points in 2024, as a tie. Recent CNN surveys put the Democrats ahead in Texas, Kansas and Maine.
Recent US political history is littered with examples where public opinion polls, even ones just days before an election, were off the mark. Trump outperformed predictions on his way to White House victories in 2016 and 2024. His narrow defeat in 2020 came after most surveys indicated a more comfortable win for Democrat Joe Biden.
Earlier this year, polls suggested Democrat Abdul El-Sayed was poised for a double-digit win in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary. Instead it was 1%. In Wisconsin's Democratic primary for governor, the candidate that had a polling lead that approached 20 points lost by a fraction of a percent.
Democrats have an identity crisis - it won't be an easy fix
According to Clifford Young, president of Ipsos Public Affairs, which conducts political and market research surveys, polling has become difficult in recent years because it's harder to reach Americans as they abandon their land lines and screen their calls. And many of those who pollsters do contact have become less willing to participate.
"Conservatives, especially those on the far right, are much more anti-establishment by nature," Young says. "And they don't participate in anything. They hate the system. That's the challenge."
If Republican voters are being undercounted in a systematic way, and polling companies don't take that into consideration when constructing their voting models, it could skew their data towards the Democrats.
That's one of the reasons why it has become trickier for pollsters to predict what the electorate will look like.

Scientists discover a surprising brain benefit of eating peanuts every day
Date:November 1, 2026Source:The Peanut InstituteSummary:A surprising new study suggests that eating peanuts every day could help support brain health and memory in older adults. Researchers found that consuming about two servings of unsalted, skin-roasted peanuts daily for 16 weeks improved insulin responsiveness in brain regions important for memory, a function that often weakens with age and has been linked to Alzheimer's disease.Share:FacebookTwitterPinterestLinkedINEmailFULL STORYEating peanuts every day may help protect the aging brain by improving insulin responsiveness in regions critical for memory. Credit: AI/ScienceDaily.com
Eating peanuts every day may offer surprising benefits for the aging brain. Researchers at Maastricht University Medical Center in the Netherlands have found that regularly consuming unsalted, skin-roasted peanuts can improve how certain brain regions respond to insulin in older adults. The findings come from the Institute of Nutrition and Translational Research in Metabolism (NUTRIM) and were published in the peer-reviewed journalFood & Function.
Although insulin is best known for regulating blood sugar, it also plays an essential role in the brain. It helps nerve cells grow, survive, and communicate with one another, supporting memory and other cognitive abilities. Healthy insulin signaling may also help protect against processes associated with Alzheimer's disease.
After participants consumed peanuts daily for 16 weeks, researchers observed improved insulin responsiveness in a group of brain regions in the right hemisphere. These included portions of the lingual gyrus, hippocampus, parahippocampal gyrus, and posterior cingulate gyrus, all of which contribute to memory-related processes.
"The hormone insulin plays an important role in the brain, where it supports memory and other cognitive processes. As people age, the brain may become less responsive to insulin, which has been linked to age-related cognitive decline," says Dr. Peter Joris, the study's senior author and an associate professor in the Department of Nutrition and Movement Sciences, NUTRIM, Maastricht University Medical Center. "Our study found that daily peanut consumption beneficially affected insulin responsiveness in memory-related brain regions in older adults. These findings suggest that enhanced regional brain insulin responsiveness may contribute to the cognitive benefits of unsalted, skin-roasted peanut intake."
Daily Peanuts Linked to Better Memory and Brain Blood Flow
The study included 31 healthy adults between the ages of 60 and 75. During the peanut consumption phase, participants ate 60 grams (approximately two servings) of peanuts each day for 16 weeks. Researchers used a randomized, controlled crossover trial, a rigorous study design that allowed them to compare the effects of eating peanuts with those of avoiding them.
The new findings build on earlier research by Joris published in 2025. That investigation found that consuming peanuts for 16 weeks increased overall cerebral blood flow (CBF) by 3.6% and improved verbal memory performance by 5.8%.
Cerebral blood flow measures how much blood circulates through the brain, carrying oxygen and nutrients that brain cells need to function properly. It is an important indicator of the health of the brain's blood vessels. Those earlier results appeared in the peer-reviewed journalClinical Nutrition.
How Scientists Measured the Effects of Peanuts on the Brain
One distinguishing feature of the NUTRIM research was its combination of a carefully controlled dietary intervention lasting several months with sophisticated brain imaging technology.
To examine changes in brain function, researchers used arterial spin labeling magnetic resonance imaging (ASL-MRI), a technique that measures blood flow in different regions of the brain. They evaluated insulin responsiveness by tracking changes in regional cerebral blood flow after insulin was administered through the nose.
The team also used abdominal MRI scans to measure fat accumulation in the liver, known as intrahepatic lipid (IHL) content. Cognitive abilities were assessed using the Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery (CANTAB), a standardized collection of computerized tests.
Researchers believe several components of peanuts may contribute to their observed effects on brain health, rather than any single nutrient being responsible.
"Multiple nutrients present in peanuts, including unsaturated fats, dietary fiber, vitamins and minerals and bioactive phytochemicals, could potentially contribute to the observed brain benefits," says Joris. "Peanuts are also a good source of plant-based protein and are especially rich in L-arginine. L-arginine is a key precursor of nitric oxide (NO), which has been reported to facilitate learning and memory performance."
What Participants Ate During the 16-Week Study
To ensure participants consumed a consistent amount, researchers supplied premeasured packets of skin-roasted peanuts throughout the peanut intervention period.
Participants were instructed to eat their peanuts in the morning or afternoon, but they could choose how to incorporate them into their daily routine. They could consume the entire portion at once, divide it into smaller amounts throughout the day, or include the peanuts in their meals.
During the control phase, participants avoided peanuts entirely. After 16 weeks, they switched to the opposite study condition, allowing researchers to compare brain health measurements under both dietary approaches.
The study was led by principal investigator Associate Professor Dr. Peter J. Joris and conducted by Ph.D. candidate Lucia Kerkhof of the Department of Nutrition and Movement Sciences at Maastricht University Medical Center.
Funding was provided by The Peanut Institute Foundation. According to the researchers, the foundation had no involvement in designing or conducting the study, analyzing or interpreting the results, or preparing the manuscript.

Nhìn lại trận chung kết, Anh Đức cho rằng vẫn có những thời điểm bản thân có thể làm tốt hơn. Ở phần thi Vượt chướng ngại vật, nam sinh đã suy nghĩ đến các dữ liệu và từng nghĩ đến từ khóa "học", nhưng chưa tìm ra đáp án chính xác là "tự học".
Trong phần thi Về đích, với một câu hỏi toán học, Anh Đức thừa nhận đã tính toán hơi vội vàng, chưa thật sự cẩn thận. Nam sinh cũng cho biết có những thời điểm chưa chắc chắn với đáp án nên đã không bấm chuông.
Dù vậy, với tổng điểm 240, Anh Đức đã giành chiến thắng chung cuộc, trở thành chủ nhân vòng nguyệt quế Đường lên đỉnh Olympia năm thứ 26.
Anh Đức vô địch Olympia 2026 (Ảnh: Minh Phong).
Bên cạnh bản lĩnh và khả năng xử lý câu hỏi tại sân chơi Đường lên đỉnh Olympia, Đoàn Lê Anh Đức cũng chia sẻ bí quyết xây dựng nền tảng kiến thức mà em đã duy trì trong nhiều năm học tập.
Theo Anh Đức, ngay từ nhỏ, em đã hình thành thói quen đọc và chủ động tìm hiểu những kiến thức mới trên Wikipedia (dự án bách khoa toàn thư mở). Đây là một trong những cách giúp nam sinh tiếp cận nhiều lĩnh vực khác nhau, mở rộng hiểu biết và tích lũy tri thức một cách thường xuyên.
Bên cạnh việc đọc, Anh Đức dành thời gian tham gia ôn luyện, chuẩn bị cho các cuộc thi kiến thức ở nhiều cấp độ. Qua mỗi sân chơi, em có thêm cơ hội củng cố kiến thức, làm quen với nhiều dạng câu hỏi và tích lũy kinh nghiệm thi đấu.
Nam sinh cho biết, quãng thời gian ôn thi vào trường chuyên cũng là một dấu mốc quan trọng, giúp em củng cố kiến thức ở nhiều môn học. Quá trình học tập và chuẩn bị này góp phần xây dựng nền tảng để em tự tin hơn khi bước vào các cuộc thi đòi hỏi vốn hiểu biết rộng như Đường lên đỉnh Olympia.
Các bạn cùng trường đến cổ vũ cho Đoàn Lê Anh Đức tại trường quay của VTV (Ảnh: VTV).
Ngoài ra, sau khi giành chiến thắng ở cấp trường để đại diện dự thi Đường lên đỉnh Olympia 2026, Đoàn Lê Anh Đức cho biết đã có khoảng thời gian chuẩn bị kỹ lưỡng để chinh phục vòng nguyệt quế năm nay.

Sau cuộc thi, Quang Minh dự định dành thời gian nghỉ ngơi, ở bên gia đình sau quãng thời gian dài tập trung cho việc ôn luyện và thi đấu.
Các thí sinh tại trận chung kết Đường lên đỉnh Olympia năm thứ 2026 (Ảnh: VTV).

Nam sinh hy vọng những thế hệ học sinh tiếp theo sẽ tiếp tục nỗ lực, mang thêm nhiều cầu truyền hình chung kết Đường lên đỉnh Olympia về với Khánh Hòa. Nhìn lại phần thi của mình, Gia Bảo cho biết em có chút tiếc nuối ở phần Tăng tốc.
Thí sinh Trần Võ Gia Bảo (Ảnh: VTV).

Nam sinh chia sẻ có những khoảnh khắc có thể làm tốt hơn nhưng chưa tận dụng được cơ hội. Đặc biệt, ở phần thi Tăng tốc, câu hỏi thứ ba khiến em khá rối và không thể đưa ra câu trả lời như mong muốn.
Thái Dương gửi lời xin lỗi đến những người đã cổ vũ, tiếp sức cho mình vì chưa thể giành chiến thắng chung cuộc. Tuy nhiên, em cũng bày tỏ sự xúc động, trân trọng trước tình cảm mà thầy cô, bạn bè và người dân quê nhà dành cho mình.
Nam sinh hy vọng những thế hệ học sinh tiếp theo của tỉnh nhà sẽ tiếp tục nỗ lực, đạt thành tích tốt hơn và mang vòng nguyệt quế chung kết Đường lên đỉnh Olympia về với Phú Thọ.

Từng mê toán, rẽ sang học chuyên sử, có thể hát quốc ca của 136 quốc gia và dành 6 năm nuôi giấc mơĐường lên đỉnh Olympia, Đoàn Lê Anh Đức đã viết nên hành trình đáng nhớ bằng tri thức, sự tò mò và bản lĩnh.
Sáng 1.11, Đoàn Lê Anh Đức (Trường THPT chuyên Hà Nội - Amsterdam) đã vô địchĐường lên đỉnh Olympia 2026với 240 điểm. Chia sẻ cảm xúc sau khi trở thành quán quân, Đức nói: "Em rất vui và khá là xúc động khi nhớ lại hành trình đã đi qua. Hành trình ấy là nỗ lực không ngừng của bản thân. Em cảm ơn chân thành tới gia đình, thầy cô, bạn bè".
"Điều quan trọng tạo nên chiến thắng của em, trước hết là sự ủng hộ và giúp đỡ của mọi người và nỗ lực của bản thân suốt những năm qua đã được đền đáp. Về chuyên môn, trước trận chung kết, em thấy mình là thí sinh duy nhất học chuyên sử, thì đấy là thế mạnh rất riêng mình cần tận dụng", Đức nói tiếp.
Nam sinh Trường THPT chuyên Hà Nội - Amsterdam cũng nhắc đến 3 khoảnh khắc tiếc nuối trong trận chung kết: "Một là trong phần thi vượt chướng ngại vật, khi có hàng ngang Bác Hồ, em thấy chữ học nhưng em lại nghĩ là đi học, khi Trần Võ Gia Bảo bấm chuông thì em thấy bạn có suy luận tuyệt vời. Hai là ở câu toán đầu tiên trong về đích, không quá khó nhưng em hơi ẩu nên tính thiếu trường hợp, Lý Thái Dương đã giành điểm câu đó. Ba là tình huống câu hỏi tiếng Anh, em đã nghe đến một chi tiết, vì không chắc nên em không bấm chuông".
Ông Nguyễn Thanh Lâm, Ủy viên T.Ư Đảng, Tổng giám đốc Đài Truyền hình Việt Nam(bìa phải)và ông Trần Bá Dương, Chủ tịch Hội đồng quản trị Công ty cổ phần Tập đoàn Trường Hải (THACO), trao giải thưởng cho các thí sinh
Đức cho biết: "Em đang muốn bình tâm một chút sau cả hành trình chinh phụcvòng nguyệt quế Đường lên đỉnh Olympia 2026. Khi MC công bố nhà vô địch, trong suy nghĩ đầu tiên, có một điều em rất vui là Trường THPT chuyên Hà Nội - Amsterdam là trường đầu tiên bảo vệ được chức vô địchĐường lên đỉnh Olympia" (Trần Bùi Bảo Khánh, Trường THPT chuyên Hà Nội - Amsterdam vô địchĐường lên đỉnh Olympia 2025-PV).
6 năm giữ lời hẹn với giấc mơĐường lên đỉnh Olympia
Đức kểĐường lên đỉnh Olympialuôn hiện diện trong ký ức tuổi thơ của cậu bạn. "Em và bà ngoại đều yêu thích chương trình. Từ nhỏ, em đã mê các gameshow trí tuệ, đặc biệtAi là triệu phú. Khi học lớp 6, sau khi xem trận chung kếtĐường lên đỉnh Olympia 2020, em bắt đầu ấp ủ ước mơ một ngày được đứng trên sân khấu ấy", Đức chia sẻ.
Đó không phải một mong muốn thoáng qua. Đức cho hay đã dành nhiều năm theo dõi các cuộc thi, xem lại những trận đấu cũ, tìm hiểu dạng câu hỏi, tham gia các sân chơi mô phỏngĐường lên đỉnh Olympiavà rèn luyện phản xạ. "Em đã chuẩn bị choĐường lên đỉnh Olympiasuốt 6 năm", Đức nói.
6 năm ấy cũng là khoảng thời gian Đức tích lũy kiến thức từ nhiều lĩnh vực, tham gia các kỳ thi học sinh giỏi và duy trì việc học trên lớp. Với sở trường môn sử và các môn khoa học xã hội, Đức có lợi thế riêng nhưng không vì thế mà chỉ tập trung vào một nhóm kiến thức.
"Em thường tự đặt câu hỏi để kiểm tra mức độ hiểu bài, lưu lại những thông tin thú vị trong quá trình đọc và tìm hiểu. Những điều tưởng như không liên quan đến chương trình học đôi khi lại trở thành chất liệu cho các câu hỏi củaĐường lên đỉnh Olympia", Đức kể.
Đoàn Lê Anh Đức và bạn bè sau chiến thắng trong trận chung kết
Hành trình thi đấu của Đức có một dấu ấn dễ nhận ra, đó là sự tự tin và cách trả lời dứt khoát. Ở những lần giành quyền trả lời, Đức thường bắt đầu bằng câu nói: "Câu trả lời của em là…"; sau đó, đáp án được đưa ra một cách chậm rãi, rõ ràng. Không ít lần, Đức khẳng định với MC rằng mình "chắc chắn 100%" về câu trả lời. Câu nói ấy đã trở thành một nét riêng của "nhà leo núi" Hà Nội.

Sáng 1.11, tại trường quay S14 của Đài Truyền hình Việt Nam, giấc mơ được nuôi dưỡng suốt 6 năm chính thức bước vào thử thách cuối cùng. Đức giành 80 điểm phần thi khởi động, 10 điểm phần thi vượt chướng ngại vật, 100 điểm phần thi tăng tốc rồi về đích với 240 điểm, chiến thắngĐường lên đỉnh Olympia2026.
Từ cậu học trò cùng bà ngoại ngồi trước màn hình xemĐường lên đỉnh Olympia, Đức bước lên sân khấu, chạm tay vào vòng nguyệt quế mà mình từng mơ ước. Từ những trang sổ chép lời quốc ca bằng nhiều ngôn ngữ, những bài học lịch sử và 6 năm bền bỉ chuẩn bị, nam sinh Hà Nội đã có một cái kết trọn vẹn cho hành trình tuổi học trò.
Cũng cần kể thêm, cậu bạn có nhiều tài lẻ. Đáng chú ý trong đó là khả năng hát quốc ca của 136 quốc gia. Tại các cuộc thiĐường lên đỉnh Olympia 2026, khả năng đặc biệt ấy từng khiến khán giả bất ngờ. Đức cho biết yêu thích những giai điệu mang âm hưởng truyền thống, có thể hát nhạc đỏ, dân ca, ví giặm Nghệ Tĩnh bằng nhiều thứ tiếng.
